name: Basilica of Saint Stanislaus Kostka
history: Winona's Kashubian Polish community organised the parish on 2 April 1871 and built a small wooden church in 1872. The present church was designed in the winter of 1893-94 by the Winona firm C. G. Maybury & Son and dedicated on Thanksgiving Day, 28 November 1895. It became a basilica in 2011.
arch: A red-brick church with a great central dome and two towers, a fixture on Winona's skyline. It cost $86,000, then an enormous sum.
features: Its stained glass honours saints cherished by Kashubian Poles, with inscriptions in Polish.
It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

look.d: The dome has dominated the Winona skyline since 1895.
Built by Kashubian immigrants from the Baltic coast of Poland.

journal: Kashubian thrift and piety on the Mississippi. The dome says it from miles off.

quiz.q: On which holiday was it dedicated?
